subject: CLOSE statement
notes: LANDED (kb/Work PB235). GR2 is definitional - it partitions physical files into (a) Non-unit, (b) Sequential single-unit, (c) Sequential multi-unit, (d) Non-sequential single/multi-unit, and those four names are the column headings Table 14 (GR3) is indexed by, so a conforming implementation must place every physical file it supports in exactly one. BOTH halves of the previous PARTIAL are closed. THE MODEL EXISTS: `PhysicalFileCategory` (CloseTable14.cs) has GR2's four members with each definition quoted and cite-checked, and `FileConnector.Category` is an ABSTRACT property, so the placement is TOTAL BY CONSTRUCTION rather than a sentence in one method's doc comment - SequentialConnector answers (a), RelativeConnector and IndexedConnector answer (d). THE (b)/(c) HALF IS REPRESENTED: the two categories are members, `Table14.Cell` prints their eight cells, and `FileRegistry.CloseByFormat` refuses any cell carrying a symbol that needs a reel/unit-structured medium (a, b, d, f) with a loud invariant naming what a new medium must implement - so those columns are now REACHABLE STRUCTURE that no supported medium populates, not an absence. THE DETERMINATION IS DOCUMENTED, discharging Annex A.1 item 24 (which makes GR3 symbol c a required documented implementor item): docs/CONFORMANCE.md 7 now carries the A.1 item 24 row - the (a)/(d) placement, the closing operations symbol c names, and the post-CLOSE record-area realization - and 2 rows 28-30 / 33-34, which previously read as a contradiction of it, now cite that row. The placement is not a free choice and the row says why: 9.1.13.2 item 6 defines the '07' this compiler already reports for the NO REWIND, REEL/UNIT and FOR REMOVAL phrases as the status of a CLOSE that 'references a physical file on a non-reel/unit medium' (cite.py --check 9.1.13.2 -> OK, rule 6), and Table 14 prints symbol g - what makes CLOSE ... WITH NO REWIND answer '07' at all - only in the Non-unit column. TEST: CloseTable14Tests pins the 16 cells against the printed table, asserts both enums still have exactly four members (the `_` arm C# requires for out-of-range casts would otherwise swallow a new one silently), and PLACES each connector kind through the behaviour Table 14 assigns it rather than through a getter - a sequential file's CLOSE UNIT is '07'-and-still-open, reachable only from the Non-unit column, and the keyed connectors take the N/A column. Falsified once by corrupting the (Unit, NonUnit) cell: three tests red, including the dispatch's own loud arm. Design: docs/FILES_DESIGN.md D11.
